body:
We pack every order carefully, but parcels pass through several hands before they reach you, and sometimes something goes wrong: a box is crushed, a bottle leaks, an item is missing or the wrong product is inside. When it happens, speed and evidence make all the difference. This guide explains exactly what to do in the first minutes, what to photograph, how to check the invoice, how to contact us, what we do next, what the policy covers and does not cover and how to reduce the risk of damage in the first place. It follows our published [shipping policy](/shipping/) and [refund policy](/refunds/) and is written for adults aged 21 and over.

## Take photos immediately
Before you do anything else, photograph the evidence. Take pictures of the outside of the box from several angles, including any damage or tears, the shipping label with your name, address and tracking number, the damaged items where they sit in the box and the invoice inside. Our shipping policy says to take a picture of the items and the invoice included in your package straight away, and to email our Customer Support Team with the pictures, so that we can reorder the damaged items for you. Keep the packaging, including the padding, until we have resolved the issue, because it shows how the parcel was packed and how it was handled.

### Good photos in practice
- **Use good light** and avoid glare on the box and bottles.
- **Show context.** One wide shot of the open box, then close-ups of each problem.
- **Include the label and the invoice** so the photos clearly belong to your order.
- **Do not clean up** before you photograph. Leaks and stains are evidence.
- **Take a short video** if a bottle is leaking, which can show the problem better than a still image.

## Check the invoice
Compare each item to the invoice. Tick off each product, option and quantity. For missing items, note exactly which products are absent, including the flavor, strength and pack size. For wrong items, note what you received and what you ordered. The invoice lists your order ID and the items, so it is the reference we both use. If you ordered several products, check each one, because a missing item is easy to overlook when the box looks full.

## Email us promptly
Send the photos and your order ID to our support email, or use the [contact page](/contact/). You can also message us on WhatsApp or call during business hours, Monday to Friday, 8AM to 5PM Arizona time, but email is best for photos. Tell us what you expected and what you found. A message that includes the order ID, the tracking number, the date of delivery, a clear description of the problem and the photos lets us act without asking follow-up questions. Contact us on the day you receive the parcel if you can, because prompt reports are easier to resolve.

### A message that works
"Order OSV-XXXXXX, delivered on [date]. The box arrived crushed on one side and two bottles of [product] are leaking. Photos attached: outside of the box, the label, the invoice and each bottle. I have kept the packaging."

## What we do
We review your photos and the order, then arrange a replacement or other resolution under our policies. Our shipping policy says we will reorder damaged items for you when you send photos of the items and the invoice. We may ask a follow-up question or ask you to keep the packaging for a short time. In a case of a missing item, we check how the order was packed and what the carrier reports, and we tell you what we will do. We aim to resolve problems quickly and fairly, and we explain the result clearly. See the [shipping policy](/shipping/) and [refund policy](/refunds/).

## Lost or stolen shipments
If your parcel never arrives or goes missing after delivery, call us at the number on our [contact page](/contact/) or email us. Our shipping policy describes how these cases are handled, including package protection where it applies, so we will check what applies to your order. Do not assume nothing can be done: tell us what happened, and we will explain your options. For late parcels, see [what to do if your package is delayed](/blog/what-to-do-if-your-package-is-delayed/).

## What is not covered
Opened or used items cannot be returned under our policy, so a product you have used and later find unsatisfactory is not covered by the damage process. Some product types, such as Puffco products, do not qualify for refunds or exchanges even if unopened, so check the [refund policy](/refunds/) before you buy. Damage that happens after delivery, such as a bottle you drop at home, is not damage in transit. And claims made long after delivery are harder to assess, which is why we ask you to report problems promptly.

## What about leaks?
E-liquid bottles can leak in transit if they are knocked, or if pressure changes affect them. We pack bottles sealed and upright where possible, with padding, but leaks can still happen. If a bottle has leaked, photograph it and the stained packaging, and handle it with care, wiping spills with paper towels and washing your hands. Keep the bottle away from children and pets. A leaking bottle should be reported as damage with photos, and we will tell you what to do with it.

## What about devices that do not work?
A device that arrives damaged is treated like any other damaged item. A device that appears undamaged but does not work is different: contact us with a description, and we will help you troubleshoot and tell you what applies. Our guides on [why a vape will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/) and [why it is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/) may solve simple problems. Do not try to open or repair a device.

## Prevent damage
- **Choose accurate addresses** so parcels do not bounce around between facilities.
- **Be available for signature** so the parcel does not spend days in transit between attempts.
- **Open the parcel carefully** and photograph before you move anything.
- **Report promptly,** on the day you receive the parcel if possible.
- **Keep the packaging** until the matter is resolved.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### How soon should I report damage?
As soon as you can, ideally the same day. Prompt reports are easier to verify and resolve.

### Do I have to send the damaged item back?
We will tell you if we need it. In many cases photos are enough, and we may ask you to dispose of a leaking product responsibly.

### Will I be charged for a replacement?
For items damaged in transit that you report with photos, our shipping policy says we reorder them for you. We will explain exactly what we are sending.

### What if only part of the order is damaged?
Tell us which items. We deal with the damaged items and the rest of the order stands.

### What if the box is fine but an item is missing?
Check the invoice, check all packing material and contact us with photos of the contents and the invoice.

## Related
See [how ordering works](/blog/how-ordering-works/), [order status meanings](/blog/order-status-meanings/) and [discreet packaging](/blog/discreet-packaging-what-to-expect/) for what a parcel looks like. Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Worked example: a crushed box and a leaking bottle
You receive a parcel with a dented corner and a damp patch. Before you do anything else, you take a photo of the outside, then another of the label. You open the box carefully and photograph the contents where they sit. One bottle has leaked onto the invoice. You photograph the bottle, the stain and the invoice, and you take a short video of the leak. You wipe the spill with paper towels, wash your hands and keep the bottle upright in a bag away from children and pets. You email us with your order ID, the tracking number, the date of delivery and the photos. We reply, confirm what we will do and ask you to keep the packaging for a few days. The whole process takes you about fifteen minutes, and because the evidence is clear, we can act at once.

## What you can expect from the outcome
Every case is different, but the aim is always to put things right. For items damaged in transit that you report with photos, our shipping policy says we reorder them for you. For missing items, we check the packing record and the carrier's information, and explain what we will do. For anything outside the policy, such as an opened item you have changed your mind about, we explain why it cannot be covered and what other options exist. We will always tell you plainly what we can and cannot do.

### Frequently asked questions about claims
**Can I report damage by phone only?** You can call us, but please follow up by email with photos, because photos are the evidence we need. A call is useful for explaining the situation and agreeing the next step.

**What if the carrier left the parcel in poor condition but the contents look fine?** Photograph the packaging anyway and check each item carefully. If everything works and nothing leaks, there may be nothing to claim, but keeping the photos costs nothing.
